label: Oesophageal cancer

approval.note: Draft checklist from the NCG Guidelines for Thoracic Cancer (2019), oesophagus: needs a clinician's check

site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: Draft checklist from the NCG Guidelines for Thoracic Cancer (2019), oesophagus: management flow on page 16 (with the book's a, b and c tier letters), the pathology synoptic on pages 28 to 31 and the work-up line on page 4: needs a clinician's check. Tier letters are NCG's where a record's basis says so; the history, histopathology, endoscopy and resection records are proposals (the page 16 text layer shows no history, endoscopy or biopsy box), to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). The book places Siewert type II and III tumours in this flow. The system records the stage as written (the pathology synoptic names the 8th AJCC edition) and never computes it; no treatment advice. India first: the National Cancer Grid guideline is the only source.
settings_note: The setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes a stage and never decides the setting). Each record carries its tier per setting; until a setting is recorded the strictest tier applies. Draft checklist: needs a clinician's check.
